setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): Wild version, first since 10-18-74, one of only three played in 1976; A little rusty and not perfect, but a fine closer [4][6]
- **Lazy Lightning** (1 review): Noticeably faster than the reviewer is used to hearing it [8]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Opens into an expansive jam [3]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): The closing jam is a highlight [9]
- **Dancin' In The Streets** (1 review): Donna shows off her vocals while Jerry plays delicately [9]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Played with real feeling [9]

## The recordings

- **gd76-09-23.sbd.backus.14687.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 185 min; rated 3.67/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: The soundboard is degraded and the audience patches are worse; Mostly a treble-less soundboard; the worst audience patch covers the Other One space and all of Morning Dew; Donna is buried in the mix while Keith is very prominent; clarity is lacking [3][6][8]
- **gd1976-09-23.117651.pa-restoration.dan.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 183 min; rated 4.29/5 by 7 [2]. Said about its sound: Cassidy through Wharf Rat is good soundboard quality, apart from a one-minute audience patch at the end of Eyes; The Other One and Morning Dew are marred by a poor audience patch with audible crowd chatter [13]

## Around the show

- Band played with tempos more than usual, some songs slower, others peppier [8]
- Reviewer considers this perhaps the best show of 1976, with Keith prominent [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-09-23.sbd.backus.14687.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Main soundboard source passed through cassette and several generations, then DAT, CDR and lossless encoding; Audience patches came from a cassette-originated chain through DAT and CDR; D. Backus did extraction and shn encoding [1]
- **gd1976-09-23.117651.pa-restoration.dan.flac16**: transferred by Dan McDonald; source: This is a restored version of shnid=14687. It did not involve an upgrade in the source material. A short portion contains a transfer from an open reel tape I… [2]. Also: Reviewer captured it by recording a stream with an audio recorder; Reviewer notes claims about the sources being circulated from partway through the first set [12][13]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1976-09-23 Thu Cameron Indoor Stadium, Duke University, Durham, NC](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1410390262996/grateful-dead-1976-09-23-thu-cameron) [16]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1976-09-23 Thu Cameron Indoor Stadium, Duke University, Durham, NC](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1410390262996/grateful-dead-1976-09-23-thu-cameron) [17]
